title: Signature database
description: Patterns that name a function by the first bytes of its body: the FLIRT idea, in the one form this tool can check. Built by `recon sigs build` from a binary whose functions something else named, and applied by `recon sigs apply` or `recon inventory --signatures` to one whose functions nothing named. A pattern never invents a function: it names addresses the analysis already found, and it is dropped when two functions share it.

generator.description: What produced the file, for example "recon 1.0.0".

pattern_length.description: How many bytes of a function's head one pattern holds.

min_fixed_bytes.description: How many of them must be bytes a link cannot change. A pattern of all wildcards matches everything, which is worse than no pattern.

name.description: The name this pattern stands for.

size.description: The size of the function the pattern was taken from: a hint, not a claim.

library.description: What the function belongs to: a runtime, a static library, a version of the CRT.

unit.description: The object or source file the pattern was taken from, when the source said.

bytes.description: The bytes of the function's head, as lower-case hex: two characters each.

mask.description: Which of those bytes count, as lower-case hex: ff for a byte that must match, 00 for one a link may change. The same length as bytes.

problems.description: What was dropped while building the set, and why: functions too short to take a pattern from, patterns with too few fixed bytes, and patterns two functions shared.
